plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked schematic of Archimedes' Proposition 7 underwater balance (On Floating Bodies) and Galileo's 1586 wire-wrapped La Bilancetta shows 1,000 g pure gold (51.8 cm³ → −51.8 g buoyancy = 948.2 g apparent weight in water) vs 1,000 g 70/30 crown (64.8 cm³ → −64.8 g buoyancy = 935.2 g in water), tipping by 13.1 g.

teach_overlay.label: PROPOSITION 7 IN WATER: 948.2 G (GOLD) VS 935.2 G (CROWN) = 13.1 G TIP
teach_overlay.detail: Inked schematic on period paper of Archimedes' Proposition 7 underwater balance and Galileo's 1586 wire-wrapped La Bilancetta showing 1,000 g gold (948.2 g in water) vs 1,000 g 70/30 crown (935.2 g in water), tipping by 13.1 g
teach_overlay.scale: instead of trying to spot a 0.18-millimetre water rise swamped by 3 millimetres of surface tension, dunking the balance turns that tiny volume difference into a 13-gram weight difference any scale can feel
